brief:
The S&P 500 rose overnight on strong Eurozone data, while the Nasdaq fell as tech stocks declined, amidst rising Treasury yields and a stronger US dollar.

S&P 500 (+0.05% to 7709.91): Eurozone Data Boosts S&P 500. The S&P 500 rose overnight as investors took in strong Eurozone activity data, which boosted expectations for economic growth and led to higher bond yields [3]. This, in turn, supported the market, as traders became more optimistic about the prospects for the US economy [1]. The strong data also led to a stronger US dollar, which can be a headwind for stocks [4].
Nasdaq (-0.01% to 26934.06): Nasdaq Falls on Tech Stocks. The Nasdaq fell 0.01% to 26934.06 as tech stocks led the decline, with Nvidia being a notable loser. [5] Treasury yields surged, which may have spooked traders, and the upcoming Trump-Xi summit added to the uncertainty. [7]
10-Year Yield (+0.53% to 5.14): Treasury Yields Reach 19-Year High. The 10-year yield rose to 5.14, its highest level since 2007, as investors anticipate further interest rate hikes from the Federal Reserve. [8] [11] The surge in bond yields was also driven by rising oil prices, which hit $107 per barrel, and a market rout that continues to affect the bond market. [11]
USD/JPY (+0.78% to 158.69): USD/JPY Surges to 2-Month High. The USD/JPY pair surged to a 2-month high as traders lifted bets on a 70% chance of a 70 basis point interest rate hike by the US Federal Reserve, citing strong economic data and a strong dollar. This move was also influenced by concerns over Japanese yen intervention, which could lead to a stronger yen if implemented. As a result, the dollar strengthened against the yen, pushing the pair to a new high of 158.69.
Crude Oil (+1.73% to 93.75): Oil Prices Rise Amid Tensions. Oil prices rose as investors sought progress on U.S.-Iran talks, despite little sign of progress [16]. The rebound was also driven by fears of escalation in the region, with Houthis firing missiles at Saudi Arabia [17]. The move was also linked to the surge in bond yields, which hit fresh two-decade highs [11, 18, 17].
Gold (-0.22% to 4308.9): Gold Falls to One-Week Low. Gold fell to a one-week low due to concerns over inflation, which is steadily mounting [19]. Traders are watching the impact of higher oil prices and the hawkish stance of the Federal Reserve [19, 21]. However, some analysts believe underlying demand for gold is strengthening [19].
